name: Hazael
bio:
Hazael is first named at Horeb, where the LORD instructed Elijah to anoint him king over Syria (1 Kings 19:15) — one of three anointings Elijah was told to carry out, alongside Jehu as king over Israel and Elisha as prophet in his own place, together forming the LORD's instruments of judgment against the house of Ahab and against Baal worship in Israel (1 Kings 19:15-18).

## 📖 Core Story: Smothering Ben-Hadad

When Ben-Hadad, king of Syria, fell sick while Elisha was visiting Damascus, he sent Hazael with a huge gift to ask through Elisha whether he would recover. Elisha told Hazael plainly that Ben-Hadad would certainly die, then wept, explaining he knew the evil Hazael himself would do to Israel — burning strongholds, killing young men, and slaughtering children and pregnant women. Hazael protested he was no one capable of such things, but Elisha told him the LORD had shown that he would become king over Syria. Hazael lied to Ben-Hadad about Elisha's prophecy, then the next day smothered him to death with a wet cloth and took the throne for himself (2 Kings 8:7-15). He later fought Jehoram (Joram) king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah at Ramoth Gilead, wounding Jehoram (2 Kings 8:28-29). In Jehu's days, the LORD began to let Israel's territory shrink, and Hazael struck Israelite land all along the Jordan, from Gilead through Bashan (2 Kings 10:32-33).

## 📖 Core Story: Bought Off from Jerusalem

Hazael later captured the city of Gath and set his sights on Jerusalem itself. Joash, king of Judah, averted the attack by stripping the temple and his own palace of all their gold and dedicated treasures and sending it all to Hazael, who then withdrew (2 Kings 12:17-18).

## 📖 Core Story: Oppression of Israel, and Death

Hazael oppressed Israel throughout the reign of Jehoahaz, reducing Jehoahaz's forces to a fraction of their former strength, until the LORD sent Israel a deliverer out of compassion for his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (2 Kings 13:3-7, 22-23). Hazael eventually died, and his son Ben-Hadad succeeded him as king of Syria; Jehoash, king of Israel, went on to defeat this Ben-Hadad three times and recover the cities Hazael had taken from Jehoahaz, exactly as Elisha had prophesied on his deathbed (2 Kings 13:24-25).
